Prime brute subscrise.def: The total value of policies sold in a period, before reinsurance. It shows the size of the business.
Prime brute subscrise.f: Example: a €600 motor policy sold in March adds €600 to March GWP.

Prime nete câștigate.def: The part of premium that relates to the period analysed, after deducting the share ceded to reinsurers. It is the period's “real” revenue.
Prime nete câștigate.f: An annual €1,200 policy sold on 1 January “earns” €100 each month.

Reasigurare.def: Insurance for the insurer: part of the risks and premium is ceded to another company, which takes on part of the large claims.
Reasigurare.f: InaVale cedes about 6% of its premium to reinsurers.

Linie de business.def: A category of insurance products: motor, property, life, health, commercial risks.

Canal de distribuție.def: How policies are sold: agents, brokers, direct online or through banks.

Bancassurance.def: Selling insurance through a partner bank's network, for example when a loan is granted.

Broker.def: An independent intermediary who represents the customer and looks for the right offer across several insurers.

Polițe active.def: The number of policies in force at a given point in time.

Rata de pierdere a polițelor.def: The percentage of policies that are not renewed or are cancelled.

Rata de retenție.def: The percentage of customers retained; the complement of the lapse rate.

Subscriere.def: The process through which the insurer assesses the risk and sets the price of the policy.

Daune întâmplate.def: The cost of claims in a period: amounts paid plus the change in reserves for claims not yet settled.

Rata daunei.def: How much of premium income goes on claims.
Rata daunei.f: Incurred claims / NEP. Example: €700 of claims on €1,000 NEP = 70%

Frecvența daunelor.def: How often claims occur relative to the number of policies.
Frecvența daunelor.f: Number of claims / policies in force

Severitatea daunelor.def: The average cost of a claim.

Eveniment catastrofal.def: A natural or man-made event that causes a very large number of claims at once: storms, hurricanes, floods, earthquakes.

Rezerve de daune.def: Money set aside for claims that have occurred but have not yet been paid.

Timp de soluționare.def: The days from the claim being reported until it is paid or closed. It directly affects customer satisfaction.

Fraudă suspectată.def: A claim flagged for additional checks because it shows signs of fraud.

Rata cheltuielilor.def: What it costs to run the company, relative to premium.

Combined ratio.def: The most important indicator in insurance. Below 100% means the insurance business makes a profit; above 100% means a loss, possibly covered by investment income.

Costuri de achiziție.def: The costs of selling policies: commissions to intermediaries and marketing.

Rezultat tehnic.def: The profit from insurance activity, excluding investments.

Profit net.def: Profit after all expenses and taxes.

Buget vs. realizat.def: Comparing actual results with planned ones.

Abatere.def: The difference between actual and budget (or the previous year), in absolute or percentage terms.

Curs valutar.def: The price of one currency expressed in another. For a global group, it changes the EUR value of local revenue.

Efect valutar.def: The part of the growth or decline reported in EUR that comes only from exchange-rate movements, not from the business.

Capitaluri proprii.def: The value that belongs to shareholders: assets minus liabilities.

Rentabilitatea capitalurilor proprii.def: How much profit the company generates for every euro of shareholders' money.

Profit pe acțiune.def: Net profit divided by the number of shares.

Dividend pe acțiune.def: The amount paid to shareholders for each share.

Rata de distribuire.def: The share of profit paid out as dividends.

Capitalizare bursieră.def: The market value of the company.

Răscumpărare de acțiuni.def: The company buys back its own shares, reducing their number and increasing EPS.

Rata de solvabilitate.def: How much capital the company holds relative to the minimum required by the European Solvency II regulation. Below 100% is not allowed; large insurers target 150–220%.
Rata de solvabilitate.f: Eligible own funds / solvency capital requirement (SCR)

Solvency II.def: The European directive that sets how much capital insurers must hold according to their risks.

IFRS 17.def: The international accounting standard for insurance contracts, in force since 2023. The data in this set uses a simplified version.

Câștig/pierdere nerealizată.def: The change in value of an asset that has not yet been sold. For example, bonds lose value when interest rates rise (2022).

Randament.def: The annual income from an investment relative to its value.

Clasă de active.def: A group of similar investments: bonds, equities, real estate, cash.

Număr de angajați.def: The number of employees at a given date.

Rata plecărilor.def: The percentage of employees who leave during a period.

Plecări voluntare.def: Departures initiated by the employee (resignations). An important signal about the internal climate.

Engagement.def: How involved in and attached to the company and their work employees are.

eNPS.def: How strongly employees would recommend the company as a place to work. Ranges from −100 to +100.

Timp de angajare.def: The number of days needed to fill a position.

Pâlnie de recrutare.def: The successive stages of recruitment: applications → screening → interviews → offers → hires. Fewer candidates remain at each step.

Diferență salarială de gen.def: The percentage difference between the average pay of women and men, ideally compared at the same level and role.
Diferență salarială de gen.f: (Men's average pay − women's average pay) / men's average pay

NPS clienți.def: How strongly customers would recommend the insurer.

KPI.def: A key performance indicator: a figure chosen to track whether an objective is being met.

Țintă.def: The value the company wants to reach for a KPI.

Tabel de fapte.def: A table of measurable events (sales, claims, hires); it has many rows and numeric columns.

Tabel de dimensiuni.def: A table that describes the context of the facts: when, where, what, who.

Schemă stea.def: A data model with fact tables at the centre, linked to shared dimensions.

Granularitate.def: What one row of a table represents. It decides what can be calculated from the table.

Detaliere.def: Going down from an aggregate figure to its components, for example from group to region, country and line.

Cohortă.def: A group of items with a common starting point, followed over time, for example the employees hired in 2022.

Analiză Pareto.def: Identifying the few items that produce most of the effect (the 80/20 rule).

Rată anuală compusă de creștere.def: The average annual growth over several years.

Anualizare.def: Converting a quarterly or monthly value into an annual one, for comparison.

Date sintetice.def: Artificially generated data that is statistically realistic but does not describe real people or companies.

Prognoză.def: An estimate of the future value of an indicator based on history and a set of assumptions. A good forecast always comes with an interval, not a single number.

Interval de prognoză.def: The range within which the future value is expected to fall with a given probability. An 80% interval means that in 8 cases out of 10 the actual result will fall inside it.
Interval de prognoză.f: The noisier the history, the wider the interval

Tendință.def: The general direction of a series, after removing seasonal swings and noise.
Tendință.f: Here: average monthly growth, estimated by linear regression

Sezonalitate.def: A pattern that repeats every year in the same months, for example the January premium peak when company policies renew.
Sezonalitate.f: Seasonal index = the month's average deviation from the annual average

Rata daunei de bază.def: The loss ratio excluding catastrophe events. It shows the portfolio's “normal” level and is much more predictable than the total loss ratio.

Încărcare pentru catastrofe.def: The amount an insurer allows for catastrophes in its plan, even without knowing when they will happen. It is calculated from the multi-year average cost.

Scenariu.def: A combination of assumptions about the future (“what if”) and their calculated effect on the indicators.
Scenariu.f: Scenario = base + the effect of each lever

Ipoteză.def: A value chosen by the analyst, not measured, on which a calculation rests. Assumptions should be visible and easy to change.
Ipoteză.f: Here: all the sliders in the “What we do” layer

Elasticitatea cererii.def: How much sales volume falls when the price rises. An elasticity of 0.6 means that a +10% price increase loses about 6% of policies.
Elasticitatea cererii.f: Change in volume / change in price

Test de stres.def: Simulating a severe shock (a market crash, rising interest rates, a catastrophe) to see whether the company stays solvent.

Retenție la reasigurare.def: The part of a large claim the insurer keeps. Above this threshold, up to a limit, the reinsurer pays.
Retenție la reasigurare.f: Net loss = min(loss, retention) + the excess above the treaty limit

Durată.def: The sensitivity of a bond's price to interest rates. With a duration of 6 years, a 1 percentage point rise in rates cuts the value by about 6%.

Cost de înlocuire.def: What it costs to replace an employee who leaves: recruitment, training, lost productivity. Typical estimates range from 30% to 100% of annual salary.

Rentabilitatea investiției.def: The net gain from an action relative to its cost.

Segment.def: A part of the business analysed separately: a region, a line of business or a distribution channel.

Pondere.def: How much a segment represents of the total. Here, the weight is calculated from net earned premium.

Analiză de mix.def: Splits the change in a group indicator into two effects: the segments themselves improved or deteriorated (rate effect), and their weights changed (mix effect).
Analiză de mix.f: Δ total = Σ old weight × Δ rate + Σ Δ weight × new rate

Efect de rată.def: The part of the change in the group indicator that comes from the change in each segment's performance, at constant weights.
Efect de rată.f: Σ old weight × (new rate − old rate)

Efect de mix.def: The part of the change in the group indicator that comes only from the change in segment weights, for example more sales in profitable segments.
Efect de mix.f: Σ (new weight − old weight) × new rate

Matrice creștere–profitabilitate.def: A four-quadrant chart that places each segment by growth and profitability, to show what should be grown, protected, fixed or rethought.
Matrice creștere–profitabilitate.f: The thresholds are the group average

Prima medie.def: What a customer pays on average per year for a policy.
Prima medie.f: Annual gross written premium / average policies in force

Matrice de legături.def: A table showing which dimensions each fact table uses. It tells you at a glance what can be combined with what.

Dicționar de date.def: The list of all columns in the data, with their type, unit and meaning. The first document an analyst reads.

Eșantion.def: A randomly chosen part of the data, used instead of the whole. Results are estimates, not exact totals.

Punct procentual.def: The difference between two percentages. If the loss ratio goes from 70% to 72%, it has risen by 2 percentage points (2 pp), but by 2.9% in relative terms.

Punct (scor).def: The difference between two scores that are not percentages, such as NPS, eNPS, engagement or customer satisfaction.

Flux, stoc și rată.def: Three types of indicators that aggregate differently over a period: flows are added up, stocks are taken at the end, ratios are recalculated from the totals.
Flux, stoc și rată.f: Premium = flow; headcount = stock; combined ratio = ratio
